hints: Look first at what type of halogenoalkane each structure is, primary, tertiary, or methyl, and which halogen is attached.
Compare Q and R, both are methyl halides, so think about which carbon-halogen bond breaks more easily, $\text{C-Br}$ or $\text{C-Cl}$.
Compare P and Q for mechanism, think about carbocation stability for the bulky tertiary molecule versus steric hindrance for the tiny methyl molecule.
walkthrough:
**Identify P, Q and R**

P has three methyl groups on the C-Br carbon, so it is a tertiary bromoalkane, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CBr}$. Q is $\text{CH}_3\text{Br}$ and R is $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$, both are methyl halogenoalkanes.

This classification controls both speed and mechanism.

**Compare speed of Q versus R**

Hydrolysis breaks the C-X bond to release $\text{X}^-$. Bond strength decreases down the group, so $\text{C-Br}$ is weaker and breaks faster than $\text{C-Cl}$.

$$\text{C-Br bond energy} < \text{C-Cl bond energy}$$

So $\text{Br}^-$ is the better leaving group, and Q hydrolyses fast while R hydrolyses slow.

**Assign mechanism to P versus Q**

P is tertiary, so it can form a very stable tertiary carbocation in a slow ionisation step. That is the $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ pathway.

$$ (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CBr} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^+ + \text{Br}^- \text{ (slow, rate determining)} $$

Q is methyl, with almost no steric hindrance and a very unstable $\text{CH}_3^+$ if it tried $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$. So $\text{OH}^-$ attacks directly in one step, the $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ pathway.

**Match to the table**

We need Q fast, R slow, P is $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$, Q is $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$. That combination matches only one row.

options.A: Correct. Q (C-Br) is faster than R (C-Cl) because bromide is a better leaving group. P (tertiary) goes by SN1 via a stable carbocation, while Q (methyl) goes by SN2 with backside attack.
options.B: Speed is right but mechanisms are swapped. P cannot be SN2 because three methyl groups block backside attack, and it strongly favours SN1. Q cannot be SN1 because a methyl carbocation is far too unstable.
options.C: Mechanisms are right but speed is reversed. Students choosing this think C-Cl is weaker than C-Br. In fact bond strength increases up the group, so C-Cl is stronger, harder to break, and R is slower than Q.
options.D: Both parts are reversed. R is not faster than Q, and P is not SN2 while Q is not SN1. This comes from mixing up leaving group ability and mixing up which structure forms a stable carbocation.
